project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 242 (terminate a campaign when the policy selects no batch, persisting a campaign manifest)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 242 in the discovery plugin: the system terminates a campaign when the policy selects no batch, persisting a campaign manifest summarizing the completed tree. This is the caller-side termination judgement that feature 238's worker pool and feature 244's retry both defer — run_batch and retry_interrupted return an empty stream (iter(()), no slots, no error) when the selected batch is empty, because "nothing was selected" is a state the caller must judge, not the pool. Feature 242 is that caller: when the policy's selected batch is empty (or the round cap is reached with nothing left to expand), the orchestrator pronounces the campaign complete and persists a manifest that summarizes the tree it walked — the branch count, the refine count, the leaf count, the node count, the deepest depth and the number of distinct theme roots, together with the campaign's calibration_status. The manifest is a consumed artifact: feature 235's plan_grid derives its branch and refine counts from prior campaign manifests, and feature 243 reads the manifest's calibration_status to refuse a VOID campaign when adding completed campaigns to the replay pool. A new module packages/discovery/src/discovery/manifest.py owns the value and its self-initializing store; the store brings its own campaign_manifest table into being on first use (the writer owns its table, as the ledger does, so no migration is touched — migrations are core-task territory and out of scope). No new @register component is added: the manifest is a value the loop persists and a reader consumes, not a policy decision the factory must discover. It depends on feature 240 (the node table holds the attempts the census counts) and stays on the discovery member's stance: stdlib only, frozen dataclasses, no cross-member imports, the node tree consumed as data through a read-only census, and every refusal naming what it refused.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/discovery member, import discovery) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions)
existing_context.test_baseline: discovery suite under packages/discovery/tests/ (test_campaign, test_workers, test_expansion, test_persist, test_retry, test_themes, test_cross_member, test_component) plus the seat suite at src/app/modules/discovery; stdlib-only modules
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, @register only in the package __init__ (never a submodule), degrade-don't-break composition, and no member importing another. The discovery member already holds the campaign record writer (feature 232, campaign.py), the worker pool (feature 238, workers.py), node expansion (feature 239, expansion.py), attempt persistence (feature 240, persist.py), idempotent retry (feature 244, retry.py), the legal theme set (feature 241, themes.py) and the shared error taxonomy (errors.py); each restates the sqlite path translation, the node-id canonicalization and the sqlite_master probe rather than importing a sibling. The seat src/app/modules/discovery/__init__.py re-exports the one registered component "discovery". Tests assert on observed behaviour with long narrative docstrings explaining the "why".

feature.description: System constructs a frozen CampaignManifest value carrying a campaign_id, a calibration_status, a branch_count, a refine_count, a leaf_count, a node_count, a depth_max and a theme_roots, refusing a non-integer or negative count and a node_count below one with a named error message

System classifies each node of a completed campaign's tree as a root, an internal refinement or a leaf from its parent_id and returns a tree summary carrying the branch_count, the refine_count, the leaf_count, the node_count, the depth_max and the theme_roots

System terminates a campaign only when its tree holds no open node, refusing a campaign whose frontier is not empty with a named ordering error message because the policy has then selected no batch and every selected node has been expanded

System persists a completed campaign's manifest into a campaign_manifest store that self-initializes its own table on first use, writing one row keyed on the campaign_id and carrying the calibration_status, the branch_count, the refine_count, the leaf_count, the node_count, the depth_max and the theme_roots
System reads a stored campaign manifest back by its campaign_id and returns the calibration_status and the full tree summary so a replay-pool gate can refuse a campaign the calibration left voided

System exposes a module-level finish_campaign function that resolves the store from DATABASE_URL and terminates one campaign, refusing by name a call that carries no database with a named error message so the orchestrator's termination never silently skips its write

System passes an end-to-end test in which a completed campaign whose frontier is empty terminates, persisting a manifest that carries the branch_count, the refine_count, the leaf_count, the node_count, the depth_max and the theme_roots, a campaign whose frontier still holds an open node is refused with a named ordering error message, and a manifest read back by campaign_id carries the stored calibration_status

project_specification.integration_points: New module packages/discovery/src/discovery/manifest.py owning the CampaignManifest value, the read-only tree census over the node table, the finish() termination judgement and the self-initializing campaign_manifest store (the store brings its own table into being on first use; it is the writer of that table, as the ledger is of its own, so no migration is touched) Reuses the discovery member's existing error taxonomy (packages/discovery/src/discovery/errors.py), translating the tree census's read into the caller's CampaignOrderError at the seam rather than leaking a sibling's error class Restates the sqlite path translation and the sqlite_master probe locally rather than importing campaign.py or persist.py, honoring the no-cross-member contract Exported from the package __init__ (packages/discovery/src/discovery/__init__.py) alongside the existing symbols, so the orchestrator's termination loop imports one spelling Covered by packages/discovery/tests/test_manifest.py
project_specification.constraints: Must not modify any shared or order-sensitive file (src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/**, alembic/**) — the manifest store brings its own table into being at runtime rather than through a migration, which is both the ledger's pattern and out of core-task territory No new @register component is added: the campaign manifest is a value the exploration loop persists and a reader consumes, not a policy decision the app factory must discover, so the package __init__ gains no new builder Termination is a judgement over the tree's state, not a new count: the campaign is complete when the policy selects no batch and no selected node remains to expand, matching the empty-stream contract feature 238's pool and feature 244's retry already return The manifest's counts are derived from the actual node rows by a read-only census, never asserted by the caller, so the summary reflects the tree that was walked rather than a claim about it The manifest carries the campaign's calibration_status so feature 243 can refuse a VOID campaign from the replay pool, but it carries that status rather than spelling the VOID vocabulary — the verdict module remains the one place that word is pronounced The store consumes the node tree as data and is idempotent: finishing the same completed campaign twice returns the same stored manifest rather than writing a second row Follow the existing docstring discipline: cite app_spec.xml feature 242 and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §5 (one campaign = one discovery tree) and §9.1 (the node table and the exploration loop) All existing discovery tests must stay green; the new manifest tests green

implementation_steps.phase: Add the frozen CampaignManifest value type (campaign_id, calibration_status, branch_count, refine_count, leaf_count, node_count, depth_max, theme_roots) with named refusals for a non-integer or negative count and a node_count below one Add the read-only tree census that classifies each node as a root, an internal refinement or a leaf from its parent_id and returns the summary counts Add the finish() termination judgement that refuses a campaign whose frontier still holds an open node, pronouncing completion only when the policy has selected no batch and every selected node has been expanded Add the self-initializing campaign_manifest store that brings its own table into being on first use and writes one manifest row keyed on the campaign_id Add the read-back that returns a stored manifest by campaign_id, carrying the calibration_status for feature 243's replay-pool gate Add the module-level finish_campaign function that resolves the store from DATABASE_URL and refuses by name a call that carries no database

Add end-to-end tests asserting an empty-frontier campaign terminates and persists a manifest carrying the branch, refine, leaf, node, depth and theme-root counts, an open-frontier campaign is refused with a named ordering error, and a manifest read back by campaign_id carries the stored calibration_status

project_specification.success_criteria: Feature 242 implemented: the system terminates a campaign when the policy selects no batch and persists a campaign manifest summarizing the completed tree The CampaignManifest is a frozen value carrying the branch_count, refine_count, leaf_count, node_count, depth_max and theme_roots plus the campaign's calibration_status, with named refusals for a bad count The finish() judgement refuses a campaign whose frontier still holds an open node, matching the empty-stream contract feature 238's pool and feature 244's retry already return The campaign_manifest store self-initializes its own table at runtime (no migration touched) and is idempotent, returning the same manifest on a repeated finish The manifest's counts are derived from the actual node rows by a read-only census, and the manifest is readable by campaign_id so feature 243 and feature 235's plan_grid can consume it All existing discovery tests still green; new manifest tests green
